description: Emergency generator minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply required for Ohio licensed hospitals
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER / FUEL SUPPLY (96-HOUR): The electrical specifications and generator design documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not comply with OAC §3701-83-54, which requires a minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply for essential electrical system generators at Ohio-licensed hospitals. The submitted specifications indicate a fuel storage capacity providing less than 96 hours of generator operation at full rated load. This Ohio ODH requirement exceeds the NFPA 110 standard and is specific to Ohio-licensed healthcare facilities. Revise the fuel storage system to provide the required 96-hour minimum supply and resubmit construction documents to ODH for review.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the fuel consumption rate (gallons per hour) for all emergency generators at full rated load using manufacturer-certified consumption data; size the on-site fuel storage to provide a minimum 96-hour supply at that rate and document the sizing calculation in the electrical design narrative.
2. Show on the electrical and mechanical/plumbing drawings the revised fuel tank configuration, secondary containment, fill connections, overflow/vent, level gauging, and fuel transfer pump arrangement; specify tank design per NFPA 30 and NFPA 110 Level 1.
3. Include in Division 26 electrical specifications a reference to OAC §3701-83-54 and NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance; specify that all automatic transfer switches transfer to emergency power within 10 seconds for life safety and critical branch loads per NFPA 99.
4. Coordinate the fuel storage installation with Ohio EPA Division of Air Pollution Control and Ohio Bureau of Underground Storage Tank Regulations (BUSTR) for above-ground or underground storage tank registration; include tank registration documentation in the project closeout checklist.

description: Patient room minimum 120 SF clear with 13-ft clear dimension required; private toilet room required for new construction
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM MINIMUM DIMENSIONS: The floor plan for the proposed {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with OAC §3701-83-54, which specifies minimum patient room dimensions for Ohio-licensed hospitals. Single-bed patient rooms must provide a minimum clear floor area of 120 SF exclusive of toilet room, closet, and vestibule areas, with a minimum clear dimension of 13 feet measured between finished wall faces. Additionally, for new hospital construction, a private toilet room with water closet and lavatory must be provided within each patient room without requiring access through the corridor. One or more patient rooms on the submitted floor plan do not meet these minimum requirements. Revise the drawings to demonstrate compliance.
fix_template:
1. Revise the patient room floor plan to achieve a minimum 120 SF clear floor area measured exclusive of the toilet room, entry vestibule or alcove, and wardrobe/closet areas; confirm the minimum 13-foot clear dimension between finished wall faces in at least one direction and annotate both measurements on the floor plan.
2. Provide a private toilet room directly accessible from each patient room (not through the corridor) in all new construction; the toilet room must contain at minimum a water closet and lavatory and meet ADA accessibility requirements per the Ohio Building Code (2010 ADA Standards).
3. Include dimensioned enlarged plans for each patient room type at minimum 1/4-inch scale showing bed position, headwall equipment, toilet room, circulation clearance at bed sides and foot (minimum 3 feet clear at foot and each side for transfer), and door swing.
4. Update the room schedule to reflect the revised dimensions; identify each room's net clear area and confirm compliance with OAC §3701-83-54 minimum standards in the project code compliance matrix submitted to ODH.

description: Ohio licensed ambulatory surgical facilities require minimum 200 SF clear floor area per operating room
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ASC OPERATING ROOM MINIMUM SIZE: The floor plan for the proposed ambulatory surgical facility does not comply with OAC §3702-11-13, which requires a minimum 200 SF clear floor area per operating room in Ohio-licensed ambulatory surgical facilities. The clear floor area must be measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment recesses, column projections, and scrub sink enclosures. The submitted floor plan indicates one or more operating rooms with clear floor areas below the 200 SF minimum. Provide dimensioned floor plans confirming compliance with the minimum clear area requirement for each OR prior to ODH plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Revise the operating room floor plan to achieve a minimum 200 SF net clear floor area measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding fixed casework, equipment alcoves, column projections, and scrub sink enclosures.
2. Provide an enlarged dimensioned floor plan for each OR annotating the net clear area calculation; confirm that the surgical table, anesthesia zone, instrument tables, and surgical team circulation requirements are accommodated within the revised layout per FGI 2022 ambulatory surgery guidelines.
3. Include an OR room schedule listing each room's gross area and net clear area; reference OAC §3702-11-13 in the compliance notation for each OR.
4. Verify that HVAC supply and exhaust air quantities, room pressurization, and filtration requirements per ASHRAE 170 and ODH standards are maintained in the revised OR configuration; provide a revised mechanical room schedule if needed.

description: Comprehensive ICRA plan with class level and physical barrier requirements required for construction in occupied Ohio licensed hospital areas
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL RISK ASSESSMENT: The construction documents submitted for the proposed project affecting occupied areas of the {occupancy} do not include a comprehensive Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required by OAC §3701-83-12. Ohio ODH requires that construction documents for projects affecting occupied licensed hospital areas include a written ICRA identifying the ICRA class level (based on patient risk group and construction activity type) and specifying the physical barrier construction requirements and HVAC isolation measures for each project phase. No ICRA document has been included in the current submittal. Provide the required ICRA prior to ODH plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Complete an ICRA matrix with the facility infection preventionist identifying the patient risk group and construction activity class for each phase of the project; document the resulting ICRA class level and reference OAC §3701-83-12 in the ICRA report.
2. Specify in the ICRA the physical barrier types required for the determined class level (e.g., sealed drywall barriers from floor to deck for Class III/IV), HEPA-filtered negative air machine placement and negative pressure monitoring requirements, and construction entry/exit protocols.
3. Show on the construction documents (phasing plan or dedicated ICRA barrier plan sheet) the locations of all physical barriers for each construction phase, HVAC damper isolation points, negative air machine locations, and construction traffic routes.
4. Identify the facility infection control officer responsible for ICRA compliance monitoring during construction; confirm the ICRA plan will be maintained on-site and made available for review by ODH surveyors upon request; include the infection control officer's name and contact information in the ICRA report.

description: Ohio hospital pharmacies must comply with Ohio Board of Pharmacy regulations and USP 797/800 for sterile and hazardous drug compounding
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / STERILE COMPOUNDING: The pharmacy design for the proposed {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with OAC Chapter 4729-17 (Ohio Board of Pharmacy regulations) and USP Chapters 797 and 800 for sterile and hazardous drug compounding areas. The construction documents do not include a clean room pressure relationship diagram, HVAC design parameters confirming ISO classification of each compounding space, or documentation addressing USP 800 hazardous drug area requirements. Ohio hospital pharmacy construction must also be coordinated with the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy in addition to ODH. Provide the required pharmacy design documentation prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Provide a pressure relationship diagram for the pharmacy clean room suite indicating the ISO classification of each space (ISO 5 primary engineering control, ISO 7 buffer room, ISO 8 ante room), directional airflow, and differential pressure setpoints per USP 797 and USP 800.
2. Include HVAC design parameters on the mechanical drawings for each clean room space: supply air volume (total ACH and minimum outdoor ACH), HEPA filtration efficiency (99.99% for final filter), temperature (66–72°F), relative humidity (30–60%), and room pressurization direction (positive for sterile compounding areas, negative for USP 800 hazardous drug handling rooms).
3. Specify that all clean room construction finishes (walls, floors, ceilings, pass-through enclosures) are non-shedding, non-porous, seamless, and capable of withstanding pharmaceutical-grade cleaning and disinfecting agents; include USP 797 and USP 800 as governing standards in the pharmacy design specifications.
4. Coordinate the pharmacy design review with the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy (OBP); notify ODH during the plan review process of OBP coordination and include any OBP correspondence or pre-application meeting notes in the ODH submittal package.

description: Complete automatic fire sprinkler system per NFPA 13 required throughout all new Ohio licensed hospital construction; major renovations (>50% alteration) require full sprinkler retrofit
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — AUTOMATIC FIRE SPRINKLER SYSTEM: The fire protection drawings for the proposed {occupancy} do not demonstrate that a complete automatic fire sprinkler system per NFPA 13 is provided throughout the entire new hospital building as required by the Ohio Building Code (OBC) §903 and OAC §3701-83. All areas of a new Ohio-licensed hospital must be protected by an automatic fire sprinkler system, including mechanical and electrical rooms, storage areas, interstitial spaces, concealed ceiling spaces, and all occupied areas. Additionally, for renovation projects where alterations exceed 50% of the building value, the Ohio Building Code requires that the entire existing building be fully sprinklered as part of the project. The current drawings do not show complete sprinkler coverage. Revise the drawings accordingly.
fix_template:
1. Revise the fire protection drawings to show complete automatic sprinkler coverage throughout all areas of the building per NFPA 13 (Ohio Building Code adopted edition), including concealed ceiling spaces, mechanical and electrical rooms, and all occupied and unoccupied areas.
2. For renovation projects: calculate the estimated construction cost as a percentage of current assessed building replacement cost; if the renovation exceeds 50% of building value, prepare and include a phased sprinkler retrofit plan for the entire existing building as part of this project.
3. Provide a hydraulic design summary note on the fire protection drawings confirming the design density, area of application, water supply data (public water flow test or private supply specifications), and residual pressure at the most remote sprinkler; include in the Division 21 specifications.
4. Specify sprinkler head types appropriate for each area (semi-recessed or concealed in patient rooms, quick-response in hazardous areas); in behavioral health areas, coordinate with the architectural team to specify anti-ligature concealed sprinkler heads.

description: Ohio CON required for hospital capital expenditures exceeding $1.5 million or addition of services/beds; must precede ODH plan review
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CERTIFICATE OF NEED (CON): The proposed project for the {occupancy} appears to involve capital expenditures exceeding $1.5 million and/or the addition of new inpatient beds or healthcare services that require a Certificate of Need (CON) from the Ohio Department of Health under ORC §3702.51. CON approval must be obtained before ODH plan review can be initiated for qualifying projects. The current submittal does not include a CON approval letter or an ODH determination confirming the project does not require CON review. Provide this documentation before ODH plan review will proceed.
fix_template:
1. Determine whether the proposed project meets the CON threshold under ORC §3702.51 by evaluating the total capital expenditure against the current Ohio CON threshold ($1.5 million for hospital projects) and whether the project involves adding new licensed beds or regulated healthcare services.
2. If CON is required, submit a CON application to the Ohio Department of Health Certificate of Need Program and obtain a CON approval letter before submitting construction documents to ODH Bureau of Survey and Certification.
3. If the project does not require CON (below threshold, replacement-in-kind, or exempt category under ORC §3702.51), obtain a written CON exemption determination from the ODH Certificate of Need Program and include it in the ODH plan review submittal package.
4. Include the CON approval letter or written exemption determination as the first document in the ODH construction document submittal; ODH will not initiate plan review for qualifying projects without this documentation.

description: ODH Bureau of Survey and Certification plan review submission required with completed application, floor plans, MEP plans, and project narrative
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ODH PLAN REVIEW SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: The construction document submittal for the proposed {occupancy} is incomplete and does not meet the requirements of OAC §3701-83-02 for Ohio licensed hospital construction. A complete ODH Bureau of Survey and Certification plan review submittal must include a completed ODH application form, floor plans (minimum 1/8-inch scale), mechanical/HVAC and plumbing plans, electrical plans, fire protection plans, a project narrative describing the scope of work, and the applicable plan review fee. The current submittal is missing one or more of these required elements. Resubmit with a complete package prior to ODH review.
fix_template:
1. Complete the ODH Bureau of Survey and Certification plan review application form (available from ODH) in full, including facility name, ODH license number, project scope description, estimated construction cost, bed count impact, and authorized signature from the facility administrator.
2. Prepare a project narrative (minimum 2 pages) describing the scope of work, affected patient care areas, occupancy classification, fire protection approach, and infection control strategy; include the narrative in the submittal package.
3. Assemble the complete construction document set per the ODH submittal checklist: site plan; architectural floor plans, sections, and schedules at minimum 1/8-inch scale; reflected ceiling plans; mechanical HVAC plans and schedules; plumbing plans; electrical single-line diagram and lighting plans; fire protection plans; and project specifications.
4. Submit the complete package including applicable plan review fee to the ODH Bureau of Survey and Certification, 246 North High Street, Columbus, OH 43215; retain the ODH acknowledgment of submittal receipt for permit tracking and follow up on plan review status with the assigned ODH plan reviewer.
